message.content: {"predictors": [{"name": "Operating Expense Efficiency Ratio", "construction": "Total operating expenses divided by total revenues, calculated from the most recent annual financial statements.", "rationale": "Firms with lower expense ratios may be more operationally efficient and thus better positioned for profitability and growth.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Short-Term Asset Growth", "construction": "Percentage change in current assets over the past fiscal year.", "rationale": "Rapid expansion of short-term assets may reflect aggressive business activity or inventory build-up, which can precede future operational performance.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Dividend Omission Indicator", "construction": "A binary variable equal to 1 if a firm eliminated its dividend in the past year, 0 otherwise.", "rationale": "Dividend omissions might indicate distress, but the subsequent rebound or overreaction could result in higher returns for omitted stocks.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Relative Insider Ownership Change", "construction": "Change in the percentage of shares held by officers and directors over the most recent fiscal year.", "rationale": "Increasing insider ownership signals management confidence and alignment with shareholders.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "R&D to Market Equity", "construction": "Total research & development expense from the most recent annual report divided by current market capitalization.", "rationale": "High R&D spend relative to firm size may indicate commitment to innovation and future growth potential.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Inventory Write-Off Ratio", "construction": "Total inventory write-offs over the past year divided by total sales from the same period.", "rationale": "Frequent or large inventory write-offs may suggest operational issues or poor demand forecasting.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Share Repurchase Intensity", "construction": "Dollar value of shares repurchased over the past year divided by average market capitalization during the year.", "rationale": "Firms aggressively buying back shares may signal undervaluation and confidence in future prospects.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Accrual Consistency Score", "construction": "Standard deviation of annual accruals to total assets over the past five years.", "rationale": "Firms with more stable accruals may have more predictable and reliable earnings.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Customer Concentration Ratio", "construction": "Revenue from the largest single customer divided by total revenues from the most recent fiscal year (for firms that disclose this).", "rationale": "High customer concentration may expose firms to revenue shocks if key customers leave.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure"}, {"name": "Cash Flow Surprise", "construction": "Difference between operating cash flow and expected cash flow (predicted using a rolling regression on past five years of data), standardized by total assets.", "rationale": "Positive surprises in cash flow may indicate underappreciated operational strength.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}]}
